item.name: Hermes prompt-builder guidance constants port (data-only, byte-equivalent)
item.contract: Port the seven unbranded Hermes prompt-builder guidance constants from `../hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py` to Go as exported package-level identifiers in a new file `internal/llm/guidance_constants.go`: MEMORY_GUIDANCE -> MemoryGuidance, SESSION_SEARCH_GUIDANCE -> SessionSearchGuidance, SKILLS_GUIDANCE -> SkillsGuidance, TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE -> ToolUseEnforcementGuidance, TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS -> ToolUseEnforcementModels ([]string), DEVELOPER_ROLE_MODELS -> DeveloperRoleModels ([]string), WSL_ENVIRONMENT_HINT -> WSLEnvironmentHint. Each constant must be byte-equivalent to its Hermes upstream when concatenated (Python parenthesised string literals concatenate adjacent strings into one). The slice is data-only — no wiring into live-turn prompt assembly, no provider routing change, no runtime behavior change. Subsequent slices will wire each constant into `assembleLiveTurnPrompt` gated on the relevant condition (tools loaded, model substring match, WSL detected).
item.degraded_mode: Constants are pure data; no runtime path is affected. If Hermes drifts upstream the byte-equivalence test fails loudly so a follow-up port row can land the new value.
source_refs: internal/llm/self_help_guidance.go (existing precedent for hermes/<constant>.go file shape)
ready_when: Sibling repository `../hermes-agent` is checked out at the active commit so byte-equivalence tests can read the upstream source.
Tests can read `../hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py` from a relative path or a fixture path injected at test time.
No live network, model call, or provider adapter is required.
not_ready_when: The slice wires any constant into `assembleLiveTurnPrompt`, `gateway.Manager`, kernel, or any channel adapter — wiring is reserved for follow-up rows.

The slice ports DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY, HERMES_AGENT_HELP_GUIDANCE (already shipped as GormesSelfHelpGuidanceForPrompt), OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE, GOOGLE_MODEL_OPERATIONAL_GUIDANCE, or PLATFORM_HINTS — those need explicit Gormes branding decisions or per-block adaptation rows.
The slice deviates from the upstream byte sequence for any constant (slack, missing whitespace, stripped trailing newline) — drift here would silently change a future wiring slice's prompt text.
The slice exposes the constants under names that conflict with existing internal/llm identifiers (verify by `grep -rn` before naming).
acceptance: TestGuidanceConstants_MemoryGuidance_ByteEquivalent: extracts MEMORY_GUIDANCE concatenated string from `../hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py` and asserts equality to `hermes.MemoryGuidance`. Use a deterministic Python concatenation reproduction (parse the parenthesised literal block) so the test is self-contained without invoking Python.
TestGuidanceConstants_SessionSearchGuidance_ByteEquivalent: same shape for SESSION_SEARCH_GUIDANCE -> SessionSearchGuidance.
TestGuidanceConstants_SkillsGuidance_ByteEquivalent: same shape for SKILLS_GUIDANCE -> SkillsGuidance.
TestGuidanceConstants_ToolUseEnforcementGuidance_ByteEquivalent: same shape for TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE -> ToolUseEnforcementGuidance.

TestGuidanceConstants_ToolUseEnforcementModels_MatchesUpstream: parses the TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS tuple literal from upstream and asserts equality to `hermes.ToolUseEnforcementModels` []string with deterministic order.
TestGuidanceConstants_DeveloperRoleModels_MatchesUpstream: same shape for DEVELOPER_ROLE_MODELS -> DeveloperRoleModels []string.
TestGuidanceConstants_WSLEnvironmentHint_ByteEquivalent: same shape for WSL_ENVIRONMENT_HINT -> WSLEnvironmentHint.

TestGuidanceConstants_NoRuntimeImport: a static check (e.g. via `go vet ./internal/llm` or a deliberate `grep` in the test) confirms guidance_constants.go imports nothing beyond stdlib — no internal/gateway, internal/kernel, internal/channels, internal/runtime, or internal/provider import.
item.note: Pure parity-data slice that runs in parallel with wiring slices. Each constant becomes a building block for a future block-wiring slice in the live-turn prompt assembly umbrella. The byte-equivalence tests are the durable contract: when Hermes changes a constant upstream, our test fails and a follow-up row lands the new value. Fixtures should pin the upstream commit hash in a comment alongside each constant so divergence is auditable. Naming convention follows Go idiom (CamelCase exported names) rather than Python's UPPER_SNAKE since these are exported Go identifiers; a comment in guidance_constants.go documents the upstream Python name for grep-ability.
done_signal: Seven byte-equivalence fixtures + the no-runtime-import static check pass; `internal/llm/guidance_constants.go` exports MemoryGuidance, SessionSearchGuidance, SkillsGuidance, ToolUseEnforcementGuidance, ToolUseEnforcementModels, DeveloperRoleModels, WSLEnvironmentHint as documented; no live-turn or kernel file is modified.

provenance.note: Hermes ships these constants as part of the agent runtime. Gormes ports them as parity data so subsequent live-turn wiring slices can compose them into the system prompt without re-deriving the Hermes wording. DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY is intentionally excluded because Gormes needs a Gormes-branded identity that is a separate parity-decision row. PLATFORM_HINTS is intentionally excluded because it overlaps with existing per-channel session-context guidance (BlueBubbles iMessage row) and warrants per-channel decisions in dedicated rows.

item.name: Context-file discovery + injection scan
item.contract: Native prompt assembly exposes a pure context-file discovery helper that mirrors Hermes project-context precedence: load SOUL.md from the Hermes/Gormes profile unless skipped, then load exactly one project context source in order .hermes.md/HERMES.md walking up to git root, AGENTS.md/agents.md in cwd, CLAUDE.md/claude.md in cwd, then .cursorrules plus sorted .cursor/rules/*.mdc in cwd. Each loaded source is scanned for Hermes-compatible injection/invisible-character patterns and head/tail truncated to the context-file budget before being rendered into a deterministic prompt block.
item.degraded_mode: If profile or project context files are absent, unreadable, blocked by the injection scan, or larger than the budget, the helper returns deterministic empty/blocked/truncated evidence instead of reading live secrets, widening filesystem scope, or falling back to Python Hermes runtime services.
ready_when: The builder restates the Hermes parity contract and confirms the helper is pure Go and does not call, import, launch, or shell out to hermes-agent runtime services.
Tests can use temp profile/project directories and fixture files only; no live ~/.hermes profile, provider credentials, channel SDK, network call, or model call is required.
The row stays a prompt-context helper slice and does not replace the entire normal-turn prompt builder, provider role selection, skill snapshotting, memory recall, or tool schema rendering.
not_ready_when: The implementation reads Juan's live Hermes profile or repository context directly in tests instead of using temp fixtures.
The slice changes provider adapters, kernel turn execution, tool registry formatting, Goncho memory recall, session-search behavior, or channel/gateway routing.
The implementation loads multiple project context types at once when Hermes precedence says the first project context source wins.
Blocked context content is injected into the prompt instead of replaced with a safe blocked marker.
acceptance: TestContextFilesLoadsSoulUnlessSkipped proves profile SOUL.md is independent from project context and skip_soul prevents duplicate identity injection.
TestContextFilesProjectPrecedence proves .hermes.md/HERMES.md wins while walking to git root, and AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .cursorrules are considered only when higher-priority sources are absent.

TestContextFilesStripsFrontmatterScansAndBlocksInjection proves YAML frontmatter removal for .hermes.md/HERMES.md plus invisible-character and prompt-injection markers produce a blocked prompt-safe placeholder.
TestContextFilesTruncatesHeadTail proves over-budget content keeps deterministic head/tail text and a middle marker naming the source and original length.
The rendered block starts with the Hermes-compatible Project Context heading and remains deterministic for prompt snapshots.
item.note: Complete: TDD added internal/llm/context_files.go with a pure BuildContextFilesPrompt helper and hermetic fixtures in internal/llm/context_files_test.go. Locked invariants: profile SOUL.md loads independently unless skip_soul is set; project context uses Hermes first-match precedence (.hermes.md/HERMES.md walking to git root, then cwd AGENTS.md/agents.md, CLAUDE.md/claude.md, and .cursorrules plus sorted .cursor/rules/*.mdc); .hermes.md/HERMES.md YAML frontmatter is stripped before prompt rendering; invisible Unicode and prompt-injection patterns produce a safe blocked marker without injecting source content; oversized context uses deterministic head/tail truncation with source and original-length evidence; tests use only temp fixtures and no Python Hermes runtime services, live profiles, providers, channel SDKs, network calls, or model calls.
done_signal: Context-file fixtures prove profile SOUL loading/skip behavior, project-context first-match precedence, .hermes.md frontmatter stripping, injection/invisible-character blocking, deterministic head/tail truncation, and no dependency on Python Hermes runtime services.

planner_verdict.reason: source-backed builder-ready prompt/context helper with hermetic fixture scope

provenance.note: Hermes prompt_builder.py defines the discovery precedence, injection scan, frontmatter stripping, and truncation behavior; Gormes should reimplement the behavior in Go as a pure helper before full prompt assembly.

item.name: Progressive subdirectory hint tracker
item.contract: Gormes ports Hermes' progressive subdirectory hint discovery as a pure prompt-context helper: after tool calls that mention paths or terminal workdirs, discover AGENTS.md/agents.md, CLAUDE.md/claude.md, or .cursorrules from newly visited directories and bounded ancestors, scan/truncate the hint content with the same safety policy as startup context files, format it as appendable tool-result context, and never mutate the system prompt or prompt-cache key.
item.degraded_mode: Unreadable directories, permission errors, malformed shell command strings, URLs, git remotes, already-loaded directories, empty hint files, and over-budget hint files return subdirectory_hint_* evidence or no-op results without blocking the tool result or widening filesystem access.
ready_when: Context-file discovery + injection scan is complete, so the implementation can reuse the existing scan/truncation behavior instead of duplicating prompt-injection policy.
The worker can test with t.TempDir project trees and synthetic tool call descriptors; no real tool execution, provider call, model call, channel, TUI, or live repository scan is required.
This row adds the pure tracker only; appending hints to actual tool results after tool execution remains a separate binding row.
not_ready_when: The slice changes startup context-file precedence, injects hints into the system prompt, mutates prompt-cache identity, runs terminal commands, opens arbitrary live home directories, or binds the helper into tool execution.
The tracker loads more than one hint file per directory, walks unbounded ancestors, follows URLs/git remotes as paths, or logs full hint content when a scan blocks it.
Tests depend on current repository AGENTS.md, live ~/.gormes, live ~/.hermes, provider credentials, or platform-specific permission behavior.
acceptance: TestSubdirectoryHintsWorkingDirPreloaded proves the working directory is pre-marked as handled so startup context is not reloaded as a tool-result hint.
TestSubdirectoryHintsAncestorDiscovery proves reading backend/src/main.py discovers backend/AGENTS.md through a bounded ancestor walk and does not duplicate on a second read.
TestSubdirectoryHintsPathSources proves path, file_path, workdir, and terminal command tokens can discover hints, while URLs, git remotes, flags, and empty args are ignored.
TestSubdirectoryHintsPriorityAndFormatting proves AGENTS.md wins over CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules within one directory and renders `[Subdirectory context discovered: <relative path>]`.

TestSubdirectoryHintsScanTruncateAndPermissionErrors proves prompt-injection markers are blocked, large hints are truncated at the configured budget, and permission/read errors return no-op evidence without panic.
item.note: 2026-05-06 bounded all-topic Hermes/Honcho weakness sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. Higher-priority open rows were blocked, draft-only, or Gormes/OpenClaw-owned rather than the next Hermes-sourced builder slice: Kanban worker rows need CLI invocation/tool prerequisites, event-bus integration depends on producer rows, plugin lifecycle is still blocked by third-party-extension work, self-update is large and prerequisite-heavy, ACP bridge/discover-probe rows are owned OpenClaw enhancements, and gateway discover/probe has existing code but stale/wrong acceptance that should be refined separately. This row is the highest unblocked small Hermes-sourced weakness: Gormes has startup context-file loading, normal-turn prompt assembly, provider/auth rows, gateway/channel rows, Goncho/normal-turn memory, browser/tool progress, setup/docs/release gates, and TUI rows covered or row-backed, but lacked Hermes' progressive tool-result subdirectory context hints. Complete: TDD added internal/llm/subdirectory_hints.go and subdirectory_hints_test.go. The pure tracker preloads the working directory, extracts path/file_path/workdir and terminal command path tokens, skips empty args/flags/URLs/git remotes, walks bounded ancestors, loads only the first hint file per directory by AGENTS/CLAUDE/.cursorrules priority, reuses the context-file scan/truncation helpers, preserves blocked prompt-injection markers, returns typed stat/read/empty/loaded evidence, formats appendable `[Subdirectory context discovered: <relative path>]` sections, and does not bind tool execution or mutate prompt assembly.
done_signal: Subdirectory hint fixtures prove loaded-dir tracking, bounded ancestor discovery, path/workdir/terminal extraction, URL/git skip behavior, first-file priority, formatting, scan/truncation, and permission-error no-op behavior with no tool execution binding.

provenance.note: Hermes lazily appends subdirectory context after tool navigation so prompt caching is preserved. Gormes has startup context-file loading but no source-backed row for progressive tool-result hint discovery.

item.name: Model-specific role and tool-use guidance

item.name: Toolset-aware skills prompt snapshot
item.contract: Native prompt assembly builds a deterministic Hermes-compatible skills index snapshot filtered by available tools/toolsets: SKILL.md and DESCRIPTION.md metadata are reduced into a manifest keyed by relative path, mtime, and size; an in-process LRU cache is keyed by local skill root, external roots, sorted available tools, sorted available toolsets, platform hint, and disabled skill names; an optional disk snapshot is reused only when manifest version and file metadata match; `metadata.hermes.fallback_for_toolsets`, `requires_toolsets`, `fallback_for_tools`, and `requires_tools` hide or show skills exactly like Hermes; local active skills win over external duplicates; output categories and skill names are sorted and deduped.
item.degraded_mode: If the snapshot is missing, stale, malformed, or unwritable, Gormes falls back to a full active-skill scan and records skills_prompt_snapshot_miss or skills_prompt_snapshot_write_failed evidence without injecting disabled, unsupported, or unavailable skills.
ready_when: Phase 2.G skills runtime and SKILL.md frontmatter validation are stable enough to expose active skill snapshots and statuses.
Tests can use t.TempDir skill roots, injected platform/disabled/toolset options, and fake snapshot paths.
No model call, provider adapter, live plugin registry, semantic skill search, or skill installation flow is required.
not_ready_when: The slice changes skill selection scoring, active-store mutation, skill install/quarantine behavior, slash-command generation, or model-specific prompt role selection.
The disk snapshot is reused after any SKILL.md or DESCRIPTION.md mtime/size drift, or after platform/disabled/tool/toolset filters change.
Condition filtering treats missing available-tools/toolsets as restrictive; Hermes keeps backward compatibility by showing all skills when both filters are unknown.
acceptance: TestSkillsPromptSnapshotManifestInvalidation proves SKILL.md and DESCRIPTION.md mtime/size drift invalidates a disk snapshot, malformed snapshot JSON falls back to a scan, and write failures produce evidence without failing prompt assembly.

TestSkillsPromptToolsetConditions proves fallback_for_toolsets/tools hide skills when the primary capability is available, requires_toolsets/tools hide skills when capabilities are missing, and nil filters show all skills for backward compatibility.

TestSkillsPromptCacheKeyIncludesToolsetsPlatformAndDisabled proves in-process cache entries are isolated by sorted tools, sorted toolsets, platform hint, disabled skill names, local root, and external roots.
TestSkillsPromptExternalDirsAndOrdering proves local active skills override external duplicates, external category descriptions are included, and category/skill output is sorted and deduped.

TestSkillsPromptStatusFiltering proves disabled, unsupported-platform, missing-prerequisite, preprocessing-failed, and frontmatter-invalid skills remain out of the injected prompt while status evidence is preserved for callers.
item.note: Builder-ready tool-calling prompt slice. Hermes defines the skill-index snapshot and conditional tool/toolset filtering contract; Gormes should implement it against the existing internal/skills runtime before native full prompt assembly consumes dynamic skills. Partial TDD evidence landed 2026-04-30: internal/skills now parses metadata.hermes fallback_for_tools, fallback_for_toolsets, requires_tools, and requires_toolsets from SKILL.md frontmatter and RuntimeOptions filters prompt injection with Hermes nil-filter backward compatibility. Focused regression: go test ./internal/skills -run TestRuntimeBuildSkillBlockToolsetConditions -count=1. Upstream contract checked against /home/xel/git/sages-openclaw/workspace-mineru/hermes-agent@69d4800d agent/prompt_builder.py:_skill_should_show and build_skills_system_prompt.
done_signal: Skills prompt fixtures prove manifest invalidation, cache-key isolation, tool/toolset conditional filtering, external-dir precedence, deterministic ordering, and status-safe exclusion from prompt injection.

item.name: Ephemeral prefill messages file injection
item.contract: Port Hermes' ephemeral prefill-message behavior into the native Go turn path. Gormes loads a JSON array of message objects from an explicit prefill file setting, resolves relative paths from the Gormes runtime home while preserving Hermes-compatible env/config aliases, validates the payload without logging content, and injects copies of those messages into provider-bound API messages immediately after the effective system prompt and before conversation history/user input. Prefill messages are API-call-time only: they must not be written to session history, channel transcripts, memory/Goncho stores, debug logs, or visible TUI/gateway output.
item.degraded_mode: Missing file, unreadable file, malformed JSON, non-array JSON, unsupported role/content shape, or oversized payload returns empty prefill plus typed prefill_messages_unavailable evidence with the redacted path and reason. Gateway and TUI turns continue without prefill instead of failing startup or sending placeholder text to the provider.
ready_when: Native full prompt assembly is complete and provider-bound messages can be inspected through hermetic fake provider/kernel fixtures.
Gateway live-turn prompt assembly has a single channel-neutral path so prefill injection can be shared by Telegram, Discord, Slack, TUI gateway, and future channels.
Config/home resolution tests can inject temp Gormes homes and env maps; no live `~/.gormes`, `~/.hermes`, provider credentials, channel SDK, network call, or model call is required.
not_ready_when: The slice persists prefill messages to sessions, memory, transcript history, debug bundles, logs, or channel-visible text.
The slice treats prefill messages as system prompt text, prepends them before the system prompt, or appends them after the current user message.
The slice reads the operator's live home directory in tests, starts a gateway, invokes a provider, or ports batch/cron prefill behavior in the same pass.
The slice accepts arbitrary objects by silently stringifying them; malformed entries must degrade visibly and safely.
The slice exposes prompt contents in telemetry or error messages.
blocked_by: Python-free normal agent turn e2e harness
acceptance: TestPrefillMessages_LoadsFromGormesEnvThenHermesEnvThenConfig proves `GORMES_PREFILL_MESSAGES_FILE` wins, `HERMES_PREFILL_MESSAGES_FILE` remains a compatibility fallback, and config `prefill_messages_file` is used only when env is unset.
TestPrefillMessages_ResolvesRelativePathFromRuntimeHome proves relative paths resolve below the injected Gormes home and never from the current working directory or live `~/.hermes`.
TestPrefillMessages_DegradesForMissingMalformedOrNonArray proves missing files, invalid JSON, and non-array JSON return empty messages plus redacted prefill_messages_unavailable evidence.
TestPrefillMessages_RejectsUnsupportedEntriesWithoutLoggingContent proves role/content validation rejects unsafe entries and evidence omits the message body.

TestProviderMessages_InsertPrefillAfterSystemBeforeHistory proves provider-bound messages are ordered system -> prefill[0..n] -> prior history -> current user for both gateway and local/TUI submissions.
TestPrefillMessages_AreCopiedPerCall proves mutation of provider-bound message slices does not mutate the loaded prefill cache or config object.
TestGatewayPrefillMessages_NotPersistedOrVisible proves gateway session history, channel transcript output, memory writes, and tool/debug logs do not contain prefill message content.
Existing prompt assembly, live-turn prompt, and normal-turn e2e fixtures remain green without prefill configured.
item.note: Added by the 2026-05-04 behavioral parity audit to row-back M42. Hermes treats prefill_messages_file as an operator-visible prompt-control feature that is loaded by CLI/gateway/cron and injected into AIAgent API calls without persistence. Gormes should first port the normal gateway/local turn contract; cron/batch-specific reuse can follow as a dependent row.
done_signal: Prefill fixtures prove env/config precedence, runtime-home path resolution, safe degraded evidence, provider-message insertion order, per-call copying, and no persistence/visibility leaks across gateway, TUI/local, session, memory, transcript, or logs.

provenance.note: Hermes owns the prefill-message load/insert/persistence contract. Gormes owns GORMES_* env naming and home resolution, while preserving HERMES_* compatibility as a migration affordance.
